reforms.description: The Canada Apprentice Loan was proposed and implemented to provide apprentices registered in their first Red Seal trade with interest-free loans of up to CAD 4,000 per period of technical training, aimed at reducing financial barriers to completing in-school training.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: By reducing financial barriers, the reform encourages more apprentices to complete their training, thereby enhancing the skilled labor force.
reforms.status_evidence: The reform was announced in the 2014 federal budget and has been implemented.
reforms.importance_rationale: While it is a significant reform aimed at improving access to training, it does not represent a structural change in the system.
reforms.source_quote: To reduce the financial barrier to apprentices completing their in-school training, the interest-free Canada Apprentice Loan of up to CAD 4000 per period of technical training for apprentices in their first Red Seal trade was proposed in the 2014 federal budget.
reforms.cross_verification_note: The reform provides interest-free loans to apprentices, aimed at reducing financial barriers to completing in-school training, which supports human capital development.

reforms.description: The Business Innovation Access Program was launched to connect small and medium-sized enterprises with universities and research institutions to facilitate the commercialization of ideas and products.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: By facilitating connections between SMEs and research institutions, the program aims to enhance the commercialization of innovative ideas, thereby supporting economic growth.
reforms.status_evidence: The program was launched and is currently operational.
reforms.importance_rationale: While it is a significant initiative, it does not represent a major structural change in the innovation system.
reforms.source_quote: In March 2014, the federal government launched the Business Innovation Access Program, to connect small and medium-sized enterprises with universities, colleges and other research institutions.
reforms.cross_verification_note: The Business Innovation Access Program connects SMEs with universities and research institutions to facilitate commercialization, directly supporting knowledge transfer.

reforms.description: The Canadian government improved the targeting of government support for business R&D by adjusting the SR&ED tax subsidies and increasing direct support for business innovation, making nearly CAD 1.9 billion available over four years.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: The increased funding and improved targeting are expected to enhance business innovation and R&D activities, leading to higher productivity.
reforms.status_evidence: The reform was implemented as part of the 2014 budget adjustments.
reforms.importance_rationale: This reform represents a major overhaul of the funding mechanisms for business R&D, significantly increasing available resources.
reforms.source_quote: Budget 2012 announced changes to simplify, enhance predictability and improve the cost-effectiveness of the SR&ED programme.
reforms.cross_verification_note: The reform improves targeting of government support for business R&D through adjustments to tax subsidies and direct support, which is relevant to R&D funding.

reforms.description: Canada reformed its Scientific Research and Experimental Development (SR&ED) tax credit programme to improve cost-effectiveness and targeting of government support for business R&D. Budget 2012 announced simplifications and enhancements to predictability, with all changes fully in effect by 2014. The government made available nearly CAD 1.9 billion over four years (2012–13 to 2015–16) in new direct support for business innovation, exceeding savings from SR&ED programme improvements.
reforms.package_name: SR&ED and Business R&D Support Reform
reforms.component_name: SR&ED simplification and direct grants expansion
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Improved targeting and cost-effectiveness of R&D tax credits enhance incentives for private sector innovation and productivity growth; increased direct support for business innovation strengthens allocative efficiency.
reforms.status_evidence: All changes fully in effect by 2014; new direct support made available over 2012–13 to 2015–16.
reforms.importance_rationale: System-wide reform of a major R&D tax credit programme affecting the entire business R&D support landscape, with substantial budget reallocation (CAD 1.9 billion in new direct support).
reforms.source_quote: Budget 2012 announced changes to simplify, enhance predictability and improve the cost-effectiveness of the SR&ED programme (with all changes fully in effect in 2014). Since Budget 2012, the government has made available nearly CAD 1.9 billion over four years (2012-13 to 2015-16) in new direct support for business innovation.
reforms.cross_verification_note: The reform reformed the SR&ED tax credit programme to improve targeting and cost-effectiveness of government support for business R&D, making it relevant to innovation instruments.

reforms.description: Canada launched the Business Innovation Access Program in March 2014 to connect small and medium-sized enterprises with universities, colleges, and other research institutions to address barriers to commercialisation of ideas, products, and services. The programme provides external business services (planning, marketing) and technical services (specialised testing, product prototyping, process development).
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Facilitates knowledge transfer and commercialisation of research outputs by reducing barriers between SMEs and research institutions, enhancing innovation diffusion and productivity.
reforms.importance_rationale: Significant new programme addressing a specific market failure (SME access to research institutions), but narrower in scope than system-wide reforms.
reforms.source_quote: In March 2014, the federal government launched the Business Innovation Access Program, to connect small and medium-sized enterprises with universities, colleges and other research institutions to address barriers to the commercialisation of ideas, products and services.
reforms.cross_verification_note: The Business Innovation Access Program connects SMEs with research institutions to address barriers to commercialization, supporting knowledge transfer.

all_reforms_including_excluded.description: Canada announced the Venture Capital Action Plan (VCAP) in January 2013, a comprehensive strategy deploying CAD 400 million in new government capital over seven to ten years to strengthen the venture capital industry. The plan establishes up to four large-scale funds of funds with private sector investors and interested provinces, structured to attract private capital (targeting CAD 2 in private investment for each CAD 1 in government capital). One fund of funds was established in January 2014 in partnership with Ontario.

all_reforms_including_excluded.description: Canada phased out Labour-Sponsored Venture Capital Corporations tax credits to wind down public support to venture capital markets. Ontario completed the phase-out of its Labour-Sponsored Investment Funds tax credit in 2012, and the federal Labour-Sponsored Venture Capital Corporations tax credit will be phased out by 2017.
